War of the Worlds is a 2025 American screenlife science fiction thriller film based on H. G. Wells's 1898 novel The War of the Worlds. The film was directed by Rich Lee with a screenplay by Kenneth A. Golde and Marc Hyman from a story by Golde. It stars Ice Cube, Eva Longoria, Clark Gregg, Andrea Savage, Henry Hunter Hall, Iman Benson, Devon Bostick, and Michael O'Neill.
War of the Worlds was released by Universal Pictures on Amazon Prime Video on July 30, 2025.
Plot
Department of Homeland Security (DHS) officer Will Radford works for a government surveillance program that can monitor every person on Earth. While helping FBI agents try to find a mysterious hacker known as "Disruptor", meteors begin striking all over the planet. Large machines emerge from these, and begin attacking humans. Radford and a friend from NASA ascertain this to be an alien invasion.
The president authorizes a military response, which other governments soon follow. Despite initial success, Radford notices the machines concentrate around data centers worldwide. The larger machines then disperse smaller insectoid creatures to harvest the data inside these buildings. This allows the aliens to strengthen their machines, and continue to defeat human forces. Radford also discovers that "Disruptor" is actually his own son Dave. Dave sends him a link of classified information about a surveillance operation known as "Goliath". Reading these files, Radford discovers that alien ships had previously arrived on Earth, and that the government knew they feed on data. Despite warnings that activating "Goliath" could alert the aliens, Director of Homeland Security Riggs chose to activate it anyway. Radford confronts Riggs, who claims his actions were necessary to keep people "safe". Riggs then locks Radford out of the DHS system.
With the help of Dave and his team of hackers, Radford is able to re-enter the system. They then plant a virus to disable the aliens machines. Though it works at first, the aliens are able to shake off the virus and continue fighting. They are also able to locate most of the hackers and kill them, except Dave.
The military plans to bomb the DHS headquarters (under which "Goliath" is kept), to ensure the aliens can't access the system. With the help of Dave and his scientist daughter Faith, Radford is able to break into the bunker in time and shut down "Goliath". With "Goliath" down, the military calls off the bombing.
Some time later, the aliens are defeated, and Radford and Dave are celebrated as heroes. His crimes exposed, Riggs is arrested for violating the Constitution, and Faith is credited with using her DNA studies to ensure the aliens' defeat. Radford is offered to lead a new surveillance program that won't interfere with people's privacy, but he declines, saying "Now, I'm watching you."
Cast
* Ice Cube as Will Radford, a surveillance and threat assessment expert at Department of Homeland Security
* Eva Longoria as Dr. Sandra Salas, Will's friend who works at NASA
* Clark Gregg as Donald Briggs, Director of the Department of Homeland Security
* Andrea Savage as Sheila Jeffries, FBI Agent
* Henry Hunter Hall as Dave Radford, Will's son, a video gamer
* Iman Benson as Faith Radford, Will's daughter, a biomedical researcher who is pregnant
* Devon Bostick as Mark Goodman, Faith's boyfriend, Amazon Delivery Driver
* Michael O'Neill as Walter Crystal, United States Secretary of Defense
* Jim Meskimen as the President of the United States
Production
In September 2020, in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, Ice Cube joined in the lead role in an untitled film produced by Timur Bekmambetov, which would be directed by Rich Lee with a screenplay by Kenneth A. Golde for Universal Pictures. Universal was intrigued by the project by Bekmambetov's use of screenlife technology, described as having "the look of commercial event film but at the budget of a contained thriller", which also allowed the actors and crew members to work in individual workspaces, which was seen as useful regarding the pandemic's impact on the film industry. In October, Eva Longoria joined the cast.
In July 2025, Clark Gregg, Andrea Savage, Henry Hunter Hall, Iman Benson, Devon Bostick, and Michael O'Neill were revealed to have been part of the project, which was revealed to be an adaptation of the 1898 novel The War of the Worlds by H. G. Wells.
Release
War of the Worlds was released on Amazon Prime Video on July 30, 2025.
Reception
Peter Debruge of Variety considered the film to be a poor adaptation of The War of the Worlds, criticizing the film's utilization of screenlife elements, Ice Cube's performance and excessive Amazon product placement.
